title: Association Between Ambient Temperature and Coercive Measures in Psychiatric Hospitals of the Rhineland Regional Council (LVR)
summary: This study investigates whether higher ambient temperatures are associated with a more frequent use of coercive measures (such as mechanical restraint or seclusion) in psychiatric hospitals. The study analyzes existing pseudonymized routine clinical data collected in psychiatric hospitals of the Rhineland Regional Council (LVR) between 2018 and 2025. No new data will be collected, and no patients will be enrolled. The aim is to improve the understanding of the potential impact of high temperatures on psychiatric care and to provide evidence for future prevention and care strategies.
conditions: Adult psychiatric disorders and coercive measures during inpatient psychiatric treatment.

interventions.name:
Retrospective observational cohort

Description:
Retrospective observational cohort comprising all adult inpatient admissions to the psychiatric hospitals of the Rhineland Regional Council (LVR) between January 2018 and December 2025. No intervention is performed. Routinely collected pseudonymize

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
As this study is a retrospective secondary data analysis of an existing routine healthcare database, no individual recruitment or selection of study participants is performed. All available observation days from the psychiatric hospitals of the LVR within the predefined study period (January 2018 to December 2025) are analyzed. Therefore, no additional patient-level inclusion criteria apply.
Exclusion criteria:
